answer: Sequential spectral docking resists sybils by requiring each agent to compute a memory-hard hash chain that emits a unique opal signal signature locked to a public spiral timestamp log. Chain depth scales with claimed weight so an attacker controlling n clones must perform approximately n squared sequential steps because intermediate states cannot be shared or parallelized across identities.
